title: Introduce token-warmth-meter and batch-drop attribution
author: Marisol Vega
release_notes: Adds a runtime 'token_warmth' metric and batch-drop attribution counters; new dashboard panels and an alert to surface cold-prefix driven cost/latency regressions.
description: Context: We see a class of hard-to-debug latency/cost regressions where short prefixes or cold KV cache invocations (e.g. chat threads resumed after long idle periods) cause disproportionate per-token cost and increase GPU batch-drop incidents. Root cause analysis showed that some invocations with near-zero KV hits still get co-batched with warmed calls and amplify backpressure or OOM scenarios. Goal: provide low-noise signals to (1) quantify per-invocation 'warmth' so teams can correlate latency/cost to cache warming, and (2) attribute batch drops to the invocation(s) most likely responsible so SREs and runtime engineers can triage scheduling/kernel hotspots. This PR introduces a token-warmth-meter and batch-drop attribution pipeline.
commits: feat(telemetry): add token_warmth gauge and histogram (runtime/metrics)
perf(runtime): compute warm_score from kv_hit_rate and prefix_len in serving path
feat(obs): dashboard + panel for token-warmth distribution by model/tenant
fix(tests): make warmth meter deterministic for unit tests
chore(docs): telemetry guide for interpreting token_warmth and batch-drop metrics
changed_files: runtime/serving/kv_cache.go - compute kv_hit_rate per invocation and expose to metrics
runtime/serving/warmth_meter.go - new component to derive warm_score and labels
telemetry/metrics_registry.go - register token_warmth gauge and warm_score histogram
alerts/batch-drop-attribution.yaml - alert rule + runbook for batch-drop spikes
docs/telemetry/warmth.md - explanation, interpretation, and suggested remediation steps
review_comments: Ava Chen: Nice signal — can you clarify the warm_score formula? The PR text mentions kv_hit_rate and prefix_len but doesn't show the exact mapping.

Author (Marisol): Warm_score = 0.6 * kv_hit_rate + 0.3 * min(1, prefix_len/32) + 0.1 * recent_invocation_rate_normalized. I added inline comments and a short doc section explaining the weights and rationale.
Devon Ross: Concern: adding histogram cardinality by tenant+model may increase storage. Can we coarse-bin tenant to tier (free/prod/enterprise) instead?
Author: Switched tenant label to tenant_tier in metrics registry to limit cardinality; retained model and route labels.
Priya Natarajan: Tests flaked on CI (telemetry deterministic test). Please add a deterministic seed for mock clock.
Author: Added deterministic clock seed and fixed a race in the test harness. CI green on rerun.
ci_summary: CI run 1: unit tests failed (telemetry deterministic test) - flaky due to clock non-determinism
CI run 2: unit + integration + lint passed after fixing test harness and reducing metric label cardinality
E2E perf bench: token-warmth emissions add ~0.2% p99 latency overhead in serving hot path (measured)
alerts_and_dashboards: New dashboard: Observability > Token Warmth - shows warm_score distribution by model/tenant_tier and rolling cost-per-token by warm_score bucket
New alert: BatchDropSpike -> fires when sum(batch_drop_count) / sum(invocations) > 0.01 for 5m AND median(token_warmth) < 0.35 for same window. Runbook links to interpret batch attribution panel.
Guidance: If alert correlates to low warm_score, recommend prefix-warmup caching, request coalescing backoff, or conservative scheduling for cold invocations.
operational_impact: Metrics: token_warmth gauge per-invocation, token_warmth_bucket histogram (0.0-1.0 in 10 buckets), batch_drop_reason label on batch_drop_count
Storage: tenant label reduced to tenant_tier to limit cardinality; additional metric volume estimated at ~0.8% of current telemetry traffic
Runtime: warm_score calculation is a few arithmetic ops; measured overhead ~0.2% p99 latency on hot paths
Rollout: feature-flagged behind telemetry.optimizer=true for 2 weeks then enabled account-wide
author_tests: Unit: warm_score edge cases, deterministic clock; added mocks for kv cache hit scenarios
Integration: end-to-end invocation with synthetic cold/warm sequences and batch-drop injection
Perf: microbench harness showing <1% throughput regression; end-to-end bench showed 0.2% p99 latency overhead
security_considerations: No sensitive data emitted. token_warmth is numeric and coarse labels only include tenant_tier, model, route. Confirmed with Security - no PII risk.
Metrics endpoint rate-limited; no change to auth model.
merge_notes: Squashed and merged after reviewers approved. Adjusted metric cardinality per review and fixed a test race. Dashboard and runbook files included in the merge commit.
post_merge_tasks: Monitor token_warmth histogram in staging for 48h to detect unexpected cardinality or cost impact
Enable alert in staging, then promote to prod after 48h if no false positives
Schedule a short cross-team sync (obs + runtime) to review early signals and proposed throttling knobs
